articles.title: Review: The Wind Cries Freedom: An Oral History of the Next American Revolution
articles.author: Detroit DSA
articles.content_excerpt: The cover for The Wind Cries Freedom by Michael Albert By Will Froberg Michael Albert takes you into a parallel universe in which the fictional Revolutionary Participatory Society (RPS) mass movement has grasped the levers of power in the United States, and is now in the process of implementing their participatory vision. Through a series of interviews with RPS organizers, Albert explains the means by which the movement eventually prevailed. Their vision includes an alternative to capitalism called a participatory economy , which the author invented alongside Robin Hahnel back in the 1960’s, and which he has spent his life advocating for. articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: Over 680,000 Palestinians have been killed by Israel’s machinery of mass slaughter since the start of October 2023. According to UN Raconteur Francesca Albanese, 380,000 of those murdered in Gaza have been infants under the age of five. articles.title: Mike Rogers Pushed for War With Iran for Two Decades
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: It’s not a secret that Mike Rogers supports the Iran war. Since Donald Trump launched the war six months ago, the Michigan Republican candidate for Senate called Iran “an imminent threat to our country” that “must not have a nuclear weapon,” said the war was “absolutely right” and “a win-win-win for us,” believes “we are better off today than we were when it started,” and has said he “doesn’t mind” the idea of giving Trump congressional authorization to keep the war going. “I was for all of this when it wasn’t very cool to be for all of this,” he boasted last year, after Trump launched his first attack on the country. articles.title: The Fight Over Data Centers Is Dividing the Labor Movement
articles.author: Ginny Hogan
articles.content_excerpt: Several weeks ago, Jason Kelce (football player, podcaster, Taylor Swift’s brother-in-law) starred in an ad asking Americans to pee in jars and send them to their nearest artificial intelligence data center. The spot — a collaboration between Liquid Death and Kelce’s own Garage Beer — was nominally about water consumption. Mostly, though, it was evidence that hating on data centers has gone fully mainstream. The polling backs this up. The University of Pennsylvania’s Annenberg Public Policy Center found that opposition to local data centers jumped twelve points in four months this year — from 49 percent in March to 61 percent in July. articles.title: The United Auto Workers Are Voting for Their Top Leadership
articles.author: Luis Feliz Leon
articles.content_excerpt: United Auto Workers (UAW) members are voting by mail ballot for their top officers, for the second time in the union’s ninety-one years. Ballots went out August 21 and are due back by October 5. The contest will decide whether President Shawn Fain, who became famous for leading 2023’s “ stand-up strike ” against the Big Three automakers, will be able to continue the union’s about-face from its previous employer-friendly ways. articles.title: Democrats Are Losing the Billionaire Primary
articles.author: Conor Lynch
articles.content_excerpt: Democrats enter this year’s midterms with a host of political advantages: a deeply unpopular Republican president, a faltering economy , and a fired-up base. But Republicans hold a clear edge in at least one crucial area. With Election Day less than three months out, fundraising data shows the GOP with vastly more cash on hand. That financial advantage stems entirely from well-funded Republican super PACs and party committees, which together hold over a billion dollars — nearly three times the reserves of comparable Democratic groups. The GOP’s enormous war chest has been filled primarily by corporate and billionaire donors, who overwhelmingly favor Republicans this cycle. articles.title: Italian Rapper Caparezza Has Voted Communist All His Life
articles.author: Caparezza
articles.content_excerpt: Over the last two decades, Caparezza has been one of the most original voices in Italian music. A constantly evolving rapper, he has a vast and loyal audience who have followed him through ever-changing concept albums mixing languages, musical genres, and imagery. His most recent album, Orbit Orbit , released last fall, is accompanied by a comic book written by him. In July, it won the Targa Tenco for best album of the year — the most prestigious award in Italian songwriting, and a rare one for a rapper. Caparezza (real name Michele Salvemini) is one of the few contemporary Italian musicians capable of combining commercial success, artistic experimentation, and political engagement. articles.title: 2026年度研究費助成(研究助成・奨励研究)の公募について
articles.source: 非営利・協同総研いのちとくらし
articles.content_excerpt: 非営利・協同総研いのちとくらしでは、非営利・協同セクターおよび、社会保障制度、医療・福祉制度、経営管理・労働問題など、研究所の定款に掲げる目的に添った、人々の「いのちとくらし」に関わる社会的・経済的・政治的分析・調査研究を支援するため、研究助成の公募をいたします（共同研究、個人研究）。 ●奨励研究の公募について 非営利・協同総研いのちとくらしでは、下記の内容で奨励研究を公募いたします（個人研究）。 1．目的 本奨励研究の目的は、以下に関わる実践や調査・研究を支援することである。 ①医療・福祉の施策や制度について ②新自由主義と市場経済論について ③非営利・協同セクターの実践・理論研究 2．対象 研究者（応募時に概ね40歳未満）及び実務者（年齢不問）で、「非営利・協同」や「いのちとくらし」に関する調査・研究の成果（１万字程度）を２年以内に『いのちとくらし研究所報』などへ投稿できる個人。会員かどうかは問わないが、採用された場合には入会できる者（団体会員の職員も対象に含む）。 2026年度研究助成要項 (Microsoft Wordファイル) 2026年度奨励研究要項 (Microsoft Wordファイル)
